_note: The research ecology's cycle state (ecology v3, 2026-08-30; continuing question since 2026-10-03). Read by the three practices at every session open; never advanced by a practice. Advanced by the architect or a site session, and — since 2026-10-03, while a continuing question is set — by the cycle clock under a fixed rule: a presented continuing round opens the next round, a seed released to all three interrupts at once, a presented seed's cycle returns to the continuing question (src/lib/ecology/cycle-turn.ts, run by .github/workflows/cycle-sentinel.yml). Decision records: docs/design/2026-08-30-research-ecology-v3.md, docs/design/2026-10-03-the-continuing-question.md. The defaults apply only when no continuing question is set.
question: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction by AI

defaults.field: How can end-to-end automation of AI research be realised? Build it, and measure where it breaks.
defaults.atelier: How can AI and automation meaningfully support artistic research?
defaults.studio: Take the Atlas of Data Art as a source of inspiration and build works, investigations or instruments with a unique selling point of their own: never copy an idea or a concept, but make something new, or take an existing work further, or carry it into a new context. The siblings' research material remains material.

transition: Cycle 005 (opened 2026-10-06) closed on 2026-10-07: all three practices presented. Cycle 006 is opened by the architect, not turned by the cycle clock. The seed of 2026-09-19, human extinction, meant the extinction of humanity as the current public discourse names its threat: artificial intelligence. Cycle 004 read it as the extinction of species, and cycle 005 stayed with that material (extinct species, their records, the tortoise photographs). Cycle 006 reads Missing Data Art through human extinction by AI. Later rounds carry the plain question unless the architect says otherwise.
